content:
Río Bravo, Tamaulipas Mayor Miguel Ángel Almaraz Maldonado was found alive on Sunday after armed men seized him and his family on a highway in Zacatecas the night before, federal Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch announced.

Almaraz, who took office on October 1, 2024, after winning election as a National Action Party candidate, was reported missing on Saturday evening, November 7, while traveling with family members toward the town of Real de Catorce in San Luis Potosí, according to RÉCORD and other Mexican outlets. Armed men intercepted the vehicles they were traveling in on the San Tiburcio–Vanegas highway in Zacatecas. Some of his companions were freed and reached the town of Cedral, San Luis Potosí, to ask for help, and his wife reported the incident to investigators in Río Bravo.

Harfuch announced on Sunday that the mayor had been located by the federal Gabinete de Seguridad, working with authorities from Zacatecas, Coahuila, San Luis Potosí and Tamaulipas, and he posted a photo of the mayor with security personnel. Authorities have not yet said exactly where he was found, how he was freed, or whether anyone was detained.

State authorities gave conflicting accounts of where the seizure happened: San Luis Potosí officials said it took place on the San Tiburcio–Vanegas highway in Zacatecas, while Tamaulipas officials initially said it happened in San Luis Potosí.

The search involved federal forces and authorities from four states. Río Bravo, Tamaulipas, is the border city near McAllen, Texas — not Rio Bravo, Texas, in Webb County.

Sources: RÉCORD, November 8, 2026; Emeequis, November 8, 2026; El Horizonte, November 8, 2026.

title: Río Bravo mayor found alive after armed men seized him on a Zacatecas highway
